The idea of a “best” movie is always a matter of taste, but there are a few ways to look at it objectively: | Criterion | 2020 Highlights | |-----------|------------------| | **Academy Awards (Best Picture)** | *Parasite* (South Korean) – won Best Picture, Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, and Best International Feature Film. | | **Golden Globe (Best Motion Picture – Drama)** | *The Trial of the Chicago 7* – directed by Aaron Sorkin. | | **BAFTA (Film of the Year)** | *1917* – a World War I epic that won the BAFTA for Film of the Year. | | **Rotten Tomatoes (Top‑Rated 2020 Films)** | • *Parasite* (97 % fresh)
• *1917* (95 % fresh)
• *The Father* (96 % fresh)

• *The Trial of the Chicago 7* (score 88) | | **Box‑Office (Domestic U.S.)** | • *Tenet* – $70 M
• *The Invisible Man* – $68 M
• *The Gentlemen* – $58 M | | **Audience Choice (IMDb Top‑Rated 2020)** | • *Parasite* (8.6/10)
• *1917* (8.3/10)

• *Soul* (8.1/10)
• *The Trial of the Chicago 7* (8.0/10) | ### Why those films stand out | Film | What made it notable | |------|----------------------| | **Parasite** | A genre‑blending thriller that combined social commentary with sharp storytelling; it became the first non‑English film to win Best Picture at the Oscars. | | **1917** | Known for its continuous‑shot illusion, the film received praise for its technical mastery and immersive war experience. | | **The Father** | A powerful drama about dementia, lauded for its direction, performances, and emotional depth. | | **Soul** | An animated feature that explored existential themes, winning the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. | | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | A courtroom drama that captured a pivotal moment in American history, praised for its script and ensemble cast. | ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a film that achieved the most critical acclaim and awards in 2020, **“Parasite”** is the clear frontrunner. However, depending on your interests—whether you prefer historical epics (*1917*), psychological dramas (*The Father*), animated storytelling (*Soul*), or politically charged narratives (*The Trial of the Chicago 7*)—any of those titles could be considered the “best” for you.
